description: Put ONE block on a page, or inside a layout's column — any block in the catalogue, chosen by `type` for what the content IS: a passage of prose (paragraphs, headings, lists, a quote — `content`, one line per block, no type needed); items (a box, steps, a timeline… — `entries`); headline figures (`entries` with a value); pictures and video (`entries` with a src); a table (`table`); a chart of numbers that are COMPARED (`chart`); a diagram of what connects to what (`diagram`); or a LAYOUT, whose region ids then take blocks of their own. Send the ONE payload the type takes — the others are refused by name. Choose its look on the same call (variant, arrangement, mark), because a block that merely fits is not finished. A page is usually a heading and ONE OR TWO blocks that answer each other — a chart beside the sentence about it, figures over the story behind them — or one block on a page LOOK from set_page: a surface, or an accent picture running down one side (never a block). A cover is a page with a title, a subtitle and an accent.

arrangement.description: The SHAPE the block lays its entries out in — same fields, same count, a different layout, and a shape changes how much text fits. Per block: box: grid, list | steps: across, list, staircase, funnel, pyramid, ring; or a FIGURE — road (3–4), climb (3–5), core (3) | text: md, lg, xl, hero, sm. A figure is an illustrated shape whose count range is a LIMIT rather than guidance — a write outside it is refused — and a block wears one shape OR one figure, never both. For a chart it is WHICH KIND to draw: column — Vertical bars, one group per category. | bar — The same comparison lying on its side. | line — A value followed ACROSS the categories rather than compared between them — months, quarters, versions, anything with an order a reader already knows. | area — The line with the ground under it filled in, for a total that ACCUMULATES rather than a value that merely moves — revenue by quarter, users by month, anything where the area under the curve is itself a quantity. | pie — ONE series, drawn as parts of a whole. | donut — The pie with its middle removed, and it says the same thing: ONE series, drawn as parts of a whole that add up. | waterfall — THE VALUES ARE STEPS, NOT TOTALS — this is the one shape on the shelf where that is true, and typing running totals into it draws the wrong picture entirely. | heatmap — THE MATRIX THE PAYLOAD HAS BEEN ALL ALONG: one ROW per series, one COLUMN per category, and each cell shaded by its value. Omit to leave it alone; pass '' for the default.

axisX.description: What the categories ARE — the label under the axis, like 'Product line'. Omit to leave it alone; '' to clear.

axisY.description: What the numbers ARE, including the unit — like 'Revenue ($M)'. Reads up the side of the plot. Omit to leave it alone; '' to clear.

before.description: Block id on that page to insert before. Omit to append.

chart.description: The whole chart as {categories, series}. `categories` are the axis labels and each entry in `series` is one named line of numbers lining up with them exactly. Echo back the shape get_document gave you and change what you mean. The chart's TITLE and its two AXIS TITLES are not in here — they are three arguments of their own on this same tool.

categories.description: The labels along the axis, in the order they should read — one per column of numbers. These are what a reader compares: product lines, quarters, teams.

series.description: At most 6 — that is how many colours a theme is required to answer for, so a seventh would repeat one.

as.description: Draw this one series as a line over the bars. That combination IS a combo chart; omit it for the block's own drawing.

name.description: What this line of numbers IS. It labels the series in the legend, so name the measure and its unit — "Revenue ($M)", not "Series 1".

values.description: The numbers, in the SAME ORDER as `categories` and EXACTLY as many. Use null for a gap — a short list is refused, because "the rest are missing" and "I mis-pasted a column" cannot be told apart.

content.description: A whole passage, in order — ONE CALL, however many paragraphs. Each line is {kind, text} and each becomes its own block: text, heading, bullets, numbered, quote, checklist, separator, code. Consecutive `bullets` (or `numbered`) lines join into a single list; everything else stands alone, so two `text` lines are two paragraphs that can be moved and restyled separately. A quote line carries its source in its own `attribution` field. THIS IS WHERE MARKDOWN LANDS: a heading takes a `level` 1–6, a `separator` is `---` and takes no text, a `code` line takes a `language`, and a nested list item takes a `depth`.

arrangement.description: This block's shape, where its kind has more than one — text takes md, lg, xl, hero, sm. Omit to leave it alone; null clears it back to the default.

attribution.description: A quote's source, on the SAME line as its text — only the 'quote' kind draws it. Echo it back on an update or it is removed.

checked.description: Whether a 'checklist' line is ticked. Defaults to unticked; only that kind stores it. Echo it back on an update or the tick is cleared.

depth.description: How deep a list item is nested. 0 is the outermost and is the default. A depth more than one deeper than the line before it is clamped, never refused. Only list kinds use it.

id.description: Echo an id from get_document to update that entry in place. Omit to create one.

kind.description: One of: text, heading, bullets, numbered, quote, checklist, separator, code. Omit for an ordinary paragraph ('text').

language.description: A code fence's language, such as js, python or sql. Only the 'code' kind stores it. Nothing colours it (there is no syntax highlighter); it travels with the document and out to markdown again.

level.description: A heading's level, 1 to 6, exactly as markdown's # to ###### are. Defaults to 3. Only 'heading' draws it. Echo it back on an update or the heading returns to 3.

text.description: The line itself, as plain text. No markdown, no HTML — the theme owns the look. A newline is a real line break. A 'separator' takes none and is refused if you send one.

diagram.description: Mermaid text. The FIRST LINE names the kind of diagram and is the commonest thing to get wrong: flowchart TD (or LR) for a process, sequenceDiagram for an exchange over time, stateDiagram-v2 for states and transitions, erDiagram for things and how they relate, mindmap for one idea and its branches, gantt for bars on a calendar, quadrantChart, timeline, kanban, block-beta and venn-beta. After that, write the RELATIONSHIPS and let the layout engine place everything: there are no coordinates to set. Labels are plain TEXT, with no HTML tags and nothing that loads a picture. Newlines are real, so send the source exactly as it should read.

source.description: The mermaid text. The whole diagram, as one string with real newlines.

entries.description: items (box, steps, timeline): meta, title, body, icon, emphasis | stats (stat-row): label, value, note — value required | media (image, image-grid, image-with-text, people, youtube): caption, title, body, src, alt, focusX, focusY, zoom — src required. One flat array whatever the block; the server knows the archetype from the type. A block only DRAWS the slots in its `renders` list (describe_block); the rest are stored and reappear if you swap the type.

alt.description: What the picture shows, for someone who cannot see it. Not printed on the page.

body.description: A sentence or two under the title. Markdown: a newline is a line break, a blank line starts a new paragraph, and lines led by "- " or "1. " become a list.

caption.description: A line printed under the picture, read by everyone.

emphasis.description: Set true on the ONE entry this page is about; its siblings then recede. Not ordinal — the entry that matters is often not the first. Leave it off entirely when none stands out.

focusX.description: Framing, a HUMAN's: how far across the picture the part worth showing is, 0 to 100. Pass back whatever get_document gave you. Do not invent one — you cannot see the photograph.

focusY.description: Framing, a HUMAN's: how far down the picture, 0 to 100. Pass back what you were given.

icon.description: Icon name. Only blocks whose `renders` lists icon will draw it.

id.description: Echo an id from get_document to update that entry in place. Omit to create one.

label.description: What the figure measures, e.g. "Median query".

meta.description: Secondary label — a date, phase or category.

note.description: A qualifying line under the figure.

src.description: REQUIRED. The full https:// address of an image that is already online. There is no upload here, and a file path, a relative path or a data: URL is refused.

value.description: REQUIRED. The large figure itself, e.g. "340ms".

zoom.description: Framing, a HUMAN's: how close in, 1 or more (1 fills the frame). Pass back what you were given. Omit all three and the middle of the picture shows, which is the normal case.

iconPosition.description: Where a block's icons sit: top, lead, none. 'lead' puts it in a gutter beside the title, 'top' above it — a gutter spends width, a stacked icon spends height, so this changes how much text fits. Omit to leave it alone; pass '' for the shape's own default. REFUSED on a block that draws no icon — check `renders` in describe_block first, since a block may store an icon it never shows.

mark.description: What this block's items are marked with. Per block, the first named being its default — steps: numeral, icon, none | timeline: dot, icon. `icon` puts each item's own icon in the mark's place; SETTING IT FILLS IN A STARTER ICON on any entry that has none, so choose each entry's `icon` yourself unless you want them identical. Omit to leave it alone; pass '' for the block's default. REFUSED where nothing is marked.

pageId.description: A page id from get_document — or a layout REGION id, to put this block inside one column of a layout. add_block with a layout type returns its region ids.

reveal.description: How the text shows while presenting: words (one at a time), type (typewriter), click (each item a step). none clears it.

stack.description: How several series share a bar. 'none' puts them side by side; 'stacked' puts them in one bar so the height is the total; 'proportional' makes every bar the same height so what is read is the SHARE rather than the total. It is a SEPARATE axis from the drawing itself, so it combines with whatever `arrangement` names. Omit to leave it alone; 'none' for side by side.

table.description: The whole table as {headers, rows}. `rows` is a list of rows, each a list of cell text. Echo back the shape get_document gave you and change the cells you mean: a cell whose text is unchanged is not rewritten, so formatting a person applied to it survives. Adding or removing a row or a column is just sending a longer or shorter list.

headers.description: The top row of column headings, left to right. Send an empty array for a table with no header row. There is no header COLUMN here — a person can make the first column headings in the editor, but this payload has one axis for them, so write those cells as ordinary text in each row.

rows.description: The body rows, each an array of cell text in the SAME ORDER as `headers`. Every row needs the same number of cells; use '' for a blank one. Plain text only — no markdown.

title.description: The chart's title, as ordinary editable text above the plot. Omit to leave it alone; pass '' to clear it.

treatment.description: How the theme paints every picture in this block: `tint` drains them and dyes them in the theme's own colour, so photographs from different sources read as one deck; `mono` only drains. null shows them as they came. Prefer `tint` on stock photographs.

type.description: ITEMS — box — Parallel things with no order and no dates — features, capabilities, sources, destinations. | steps — Ordered stages where the order is the point — a process, an onboarding, a how-it-works. | timeline — Events anchored to a date or period, in chronological order. ‖ STATS — stat-row — Headline numbers — metrics, traction, results. ‖ MEDIA — image — A photograph, screenshot or diagram that carries the point on its own. | image-grid — Several pictures that belong together — a set of screenshots, product shots, or places. | image-with-text — A picture that needs explaining — a screenshot with the point spelled out, a photograph with its story. | people — People, when there are several of them — a team, a board, a speaker line-up, the customers on a logo wall, the contributors to a release. | youtube — A YouTube video that carries the point — a demo, a talk, a customer saying it themselves. ‖ TABLE — table — Values that only make sense at the crossing of two things — a specification, a price list, a schedule, a set of measurements. ‖ CHART — chart — Numbers that are COMPARED rather than listed — a trend, a split, a ranking. ‖ DIAGRAM — diagram — A flowchart, a sequence, an org chart, a state machine, an entity diagram — anything whose meaning is in what connects to what. ‖ LAYOUT — two-cols, three-cols, four-cols, five-cols, lead-and-rest: columns that other blocks go inside; its region ids come back, and each takes blocks where a pageId does. ‖ PROSE needs no type: send `content`, each line carrying its own kind.

variant.description: The block's style, a NAME the theme paints alike under every theme: plain — the theme's own default | accent-bar — a bar down the leading edge | soft-fill — a tinted plane, no border | outlined — a border on four sides, no fill | top-rule — a coloured line across the top | side-rule — tinted, bordered, with a bar on the leading edge | raised-card — a lifted card with a soft shadow | gradient-card — a card over a gradient | solid-accent — filled in the accent colour, ink flipped | leaf-corner — three corners round, one square | banded — alternate rows tinted (table) | header-band — the header row on its own plane (box, table) | accent-header — eyebrow and title on the accent, body on paper (box) | marked — the numeral or dot in a filled disc (steps, timeline) | tinted — a plane in the theme's own hue, ink to match. Omit to leave styling alone; pass '' for 'plain'.

name: add_block
title: Add a block to a page
